q: What unit owns isolation: person, agent, project, tenant, or source?
a: Repo answer: one Moorcheh namespace per agent_id, memanto_agent_{agent_id}; ordinary recall searches only that namespace (core.py:80-82; memory_read_service.py:895-905).

q: What is allowed onto the write path?
a: Repo answer: explicit arbitrary nonblank memories, accepted file types, or LLM-extracted “durable” facts/preferences/decisions/instructions/goals/commitments/errors/observations/relationships/context/events/artifacts/learnings.

q: Should ingestion be verbatim, extracted, or both?
a: Repo answer: both.

q: What ontology should a memory inhabit?
a: Repo answer: one optional type among 13; missing/invalid extracted type falls back to deterministic parsing or effectively fact at serialization (constants.py:3-18; core.py:140-152; conversation_memory_extraction_service.py:154-160; routes/memory.py:442-455).

q: Is memory a structured assertion or a searchable card?
a: Repo answer: searchable card text plus flat metadata; title/content/tags are folded into a single embedded string (core.py:133-178).

q: Who owns timestamps and ordering?
a: Repo answer: server stamps current UTC, except imported provenance may preserve valid imported timestamps; updated records preserve creation and refresh update time (memory_write_service.py:96-113,330-504).

q: What is confidence, and who is permitted to set it?
a: Repo answer: any caller or extractor supplies a scalar [0,1], default 0.8; recall may filter numerically, while unknown legacy confidence fails open (core.py:115; models/__init__.py:43; conversation_memory_extraction_service.py:165-169

q: How are duplicates defined and resolved?
a: Repo answer: extraction removes exact normalized (type, lowercased whitespace-collapsed content) duplicates within one model response (conversation_memory_extraction_service.py:141-186).

q: What happens when evidence contradicts an existing memory?
a: Repo answer: ordinary writes do not synchronously check or suppress contradictions.

q: Should corrections mutate in place, append a version, or suppress re-derivation?
a: Repo answer: edit is same-ID upsert; hard delete removes; expire preserves but can restore.

q: What should expiry mean?
a: Repo answer: expiry is reversible state, stamped with when/why; nothing expires automatically until a sweep; purge is separate and defaults to never (core.py:126-131,184-194; memory_policy_service.py:1-9,352-503).

q: What gets discarded, and is discard observable?
a: Repo answer: blank/invalid extraction items, excess messages/content/memories, invalid types (type becomes None), overlong memory tails (ellipsis), within-response duplicates, secrets/transient chatter if the model obeys, malformed

q: What is retrieved and how is it ordered?
a: Repo answer: one similarity query per selected type, merged by backend score descending; candidate pool up to 100; exact metadata filters plus client-side temporal/confidence/status filters

q: Should expired/low-confidence records fail open or fail closed?
a: Repo answer: recall defaults to all statuses; legacy missing status is active; unknown confidence survives a minimum-confidence filter; malformed expiry timestamp in historical recall fails

q: What should a caller see?
a: Repo answer: remember returns identifiers/status/type/provenance/confidence; recall returns normalized memory cards including score/source/provenance/status; answer returns generated text and backend sources (models/__init__.py:226-312; routes/memory.py:466-495,965-1109).

q: What happens on failure after the memory commit?
a: Repo answer: activity/Markdown session summary logging is best-effort and may fail without rolling back the committed memory (session_service.py:758-788,852-874; routes/memory.py:466-495).

q: What does the system do when confidence/retrieval is insufficient?
a: Repo answer: no application-level abstention policy.

q: Is observation frequency allowed to become authority?
a: Repo answer: no automatic promotion mechanism exists, but neither is there an enforced tier boundary.

q: Which operations are idempotent, and what ordering is assumed?
a: Repo answer: same-ID upload/update is treated as idempotent upsert (memory_write_service.py:460-495); UUID-default writes are not idempotent under retry (core.py:89).

q: Who may write on behalf of whom?
a: Repo answer: session token scopes agent namespace, while source is an open but syntax-bounded writer label and actor_id is set from the session (core.py:27-43,110-120; routes/memory.py:377-466).
